title: The problem-solving prizes
titleChinese: 为鼓励创新和解决问题设置“挑战奖”
paragraphs: What do you do when you have a problem? Do you go to an expert, ask your friends to come up with an idea? Or, given the chance, would you ask a crowd of strangers for a solution? It may sound strange, but it has spurred more than a few successful innovations. That’s the thinking behind a 'challenge prize'.

Challenge prizes come in many shapes and sizes but the basic concept remains the same. Rather than consulting and paying an expert to innovate a solution, you offer the prize up to anyone who believes they can solve it and present the first to do so with a prize. This might sound odd - many would argue, 'Who is better qualified than an expert?' But actually, not using one seems to result in a great deal of thinking outside of the box.

Some argue that formal education can kill creativity because it sometimes only teaches a single solution to a problem or single method to achieve a task. In the same way, some suggest that experts can suffer from tunnel vision. "If we launch an XPRIZE and it's just the 'experts' that come out and compete, they're usually the ones that will tell us it can't be done." says Marcus Shingles, former CEO of the XPRIZE Foundation, which organises challenge prizes today.

There are other advantages too. "You're not asking people to use a particular solution set on how to solve that problem. So you get this tremendous amount of diversity." adds Shingles. And because the crowd acts like an impromptu think tank, its lateral thinking can throw up issues that may have been overlooked.

Challenge prizes were most popular during the 18th and 19th centuries, but have received renewed interest more recently. Historically, many practical inventions have been conceived in this way – for example, the tin can. More recently, Virgin Galactic, a company hoping to commercialise space flight, developed out of the Ansari XPRIZE 2004 winner Tier One. They successfully launched a reusable spacecraft that left the Earth's atmosphere twice in two weeks. The prize was $10m.

However, there are dangers connected to blue-sky thinking. "You don't want to be creating a challenge prize which incentivises people to solve a problem where there is no demand," says Tris Dyson, executive director of challenge prizes at Nesta, a UK-based innovation foundation. This happened in 1979 where a Kremer prize of £100,000 was claimed by the first person to fly under human power across the English Channel. Despite its successful completion, it has not led to the adoption of human-powered flight as a form of travel. And of course, there are those who invest their personal time and money only to see no return at all: someone else claims the prize, or they find that the reward does not match the resources they invested.

The pros and cons of challenge prizes affect both problem-setters and problem-solvers. But they don’t seem to be going out of style anytime soon. To many, the challenge to innovate, the lure of the prize and the prestige of being first is too much to resist. And there’s no solution for that.

vocabulary.term: thinking outside of the box [ˈθɪŋkɪŋ aʊtˈsaɪd əv ðə bɒks] 跳出常规的思考
vocabulary.entry: thinking outside of the box [ˈθɪŋkɪŋ aʊtˈsaɪd əv ðə bɒks] 跳出常规的思考
vocabulary.example: The marketing team used thinking outside of the box to launch a viral campaign.
vocabulary.translation: 营销团队运用跳出常规的思考，发起了一场病毒式传播的活动。

vocabulary.term: tunnel vision [ˈtʌnəl ˈvɪʒn] 视野狭隘
vocabulary.entry: tunnel vision [ˈtʌnəl ˈvɪʒn] 视野狭隘
vocabulary.example: Tunnel vision prevented him from seeing the long-term consequences of his decision.
vocabulary.translation: 视野狭隘让他无法看到自己决定的长期后果。

vocabulary.term: diversity [daɪˈvɜːsəti] n. 多样性
vocabulary.entry: diversity [daɪˈvɜːsəti] n. 多样性
vocabulary.example: Workplace diversity fosters creativity and better problem-solving.
vocabulary.translation: 职场多样性能促进创造力和更有效的问题解决。

vocabulary.term: impromptu think tank [ɪmˈprɒmptjuː θɪŋk tæŋk] 临时智囊团
vocabulary.entry: impromptu think tank [ɪmˈprɒmptjuː θɪŋk tæŋk] 临时智囊团
vocabulary.example: We assembled an impromptu think tank to address the urgent crisis.
vocabulary.translation: 我们组建了一个临时智囊团来应对这场紧急危机。

vocabulary.term: lateral thinking [ˈlætərəl ˈθɪŋkɪŋ] 横向思维
vocabulary.entry: lateral thinking [ˈlætərəl ˈθɪŋkɪŋ] 横向思维
vocabulary.example: Lateral thinking helped her find a simple solution to the complex problem.
vocabulary.translation: 横向思维帮助她找到了解决这个复杂问题的简单方法。

vocabulary.term: blue-sky thinking [ˈbluː skaɪ ˈθɪŋkɪŋ] 天马行空的思考
vocabulary.entry: blue-sky thinking [ˈbluː skaɪ ˈθɪŋkɪŋ] 天马行空的思考
vocabulary.example: Blue-sky thinking is essential for developing breakthrough technologies.
vocabulary.translation: 天马行空的思考对于开发突破性技术至关重要。

vocabulary.term: spur [spɜː(r)] v. 激励，促进
vocabulary.entry: spur [spɜː(r)] v. 激励，促进
vocabulary.example: The government’s investment will spur growth in the renewable energy sector.
vocabulary.translation: 政府的投资将促进可再生能源行业的发展。

vocabulary.term: conceive [kənˈsiːv] v. 构思，设想
vocabulary.entry: conceive [kənˈsiːv] v. 构思，设想
vocabulary.example: She conceived the idea of a community garden while volunteering at a local school.
vocabulary.translation: 她在当地学校做志愿者时，构思了社区花园的想法。

vocabulary.term: commercialise [kəˈmɜːʃəlaɪz] v. 商业化
vocabulary.entry: commercialise [kəˈmɜːʃəlaɪz] v. 商业化
vocabulary.example: The startup spent two years developing and commercialising the new software.
vocabulary.translation: 这家初创公司花了两年时间开发并将这款新软件商业化。

vocabulary.term: reusable [ˌriːˈjuːzəbl] adj. 可重复使用的
vocabulary.entry: reusable [ˌriːˈjuːzəbl] adj. 可重复使用的
vocabulary.example: Many cafes now offer discounts to customers who bring their own reusable cups.
vocabulary.translation: 现在许多咖啡馆为自带可重复使用杯子的顾客提供折扣。

vocabulary.term: incentivise [ɪnˈsentɪvaɪz] v. 激励，刺激
vocabulary.entry: incentivise [ɪnˈsentɪvaɪz] v. 激励，刺激
vocabulary.example: The company uses bonuses to incentivise employees to meet performance targets.
vocabulary.translation: 该公司通过奖金激励员工完成绩效目标。

vocabulary.term: prestige [preˈstiːʒ] n. 声望，声誉
vocabulary.entry: prestige [preˈstiːʒ] n. 声望，声誉
vocabulary.example: The university’s prestige attracts students from all over the world.
vocabulary.translation: 这所大学的声望吸引着来自世界各地的学生。

vocabulary.term: pros and cons [prəʊz ənd kɒnz] 利弊
vocabulary.entry: pros and cons [prəʊz ənd kɒnz] 利弊
vocabulary.example: Before choosing a college, it’s important to list the pros and cons of each option.
vocabulary.translation: 选择大学前，列出每个选项的利弊很重要。

vocabulary.term: go out of style [ɡəʊ aʊt əv staɪl] 过时
vocabulary.entry: go out of style [ɡəʊ aʊt əv staɪl] 过时
vocabulary.example: Fashions come and go, but a well-tailored suit never goes out of style.
vocabulary.translation: 时尚潮流变幻莫测，但剪裁精良的西装永远不会过时。

vocabulary.entry: lure [lʊə(r)] n. 诱惑，吸引力
vocabulary.example: The lure of adventure led her to travel to remote parts of the world.
vocabulary.translation: 冒险的吸引力促使她前往世界偏远地区旅行。

vocabulary.entry: overlook [ˌəʊvəˈlʊk] v. 忽视，忽略
vocabulary.example: It’s easy to overlook small details when planning a large event.
vocabulary.translation: 策划大型活动时，很容易忽略一些小细节。

vocabulary.term: renewed interest [rɪˈnjuːd ˈɪntrəst] 重新产生的兴趣
vocabulary.entry: renewed interest [rɪˈnjuːd ˈɪntrəst] 重新产生的兴趣
vocabulary.example: The release of the classic film’s remake sparked renewed interest in the original.
vocabulary.translation: 这部经典电影翻拍版的上映，重新激发了人们对原版的兴趣。

vocabulary.term: impromptu [ɪmˈprɒmptjuː] adj. 即兴的，临时的
vocabulary.entry: impromptu [ɪmˈprɒmptjuː] adj. 即兴的，临时的
vocabulary.example: The band played an impromptu set for the crowd after the official concert ended.
vocabulary.translation: 正式音乐会结束后，乐队为观众即兴演奏了一曲。

vocabulary.term: tremendous [trəˈmendəs] adj. 巨大的，极大的
vocabulary.entry: tremendous [trəˈmendəs] adj. 巨大的，极大的
vocabulary.example: The project required tremendous effort from everyone on the team.
vocabulary.translation: 这个项目需要团队每个人付出巨大的努力。

vocabulary.term: qualify [ˈkwɒlɪfaɪ] v. 具备资格，合格
vocabulary.entry: qualify [ˈkwɒlɪfaɪ] v. 具备资格，合格
vocabulary.example: To qualify for the scholarship, students must maintain a high GPA.
vocabulary.translation: 要获得奖学金资格，学生必须保持较高的平均绩点。
